subject: Conditional TIA acceptance & technical evidence plan — NovaHealth pilot
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-17T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Conditional TIA acceptance & technical evidence plan — NovaHealth pilot

Team —

Following the call with NovaHealth this morning, Legal asked that we document a conditional acceptance approach for their pilot while we gather TIA evidence. I sketched a lightweight plan attached (tia-evidence-checklist.xlsx) that splits evidence into:

- Must-have (access logs, encryption-at-rest configurations, KMS provenance)
- Nice-to-have (network diagrams, bandwidth isolation statements, subprocessor SLAs)
- Defer (historical analytics not in scope for pilot)

Key asks:
- Vivek: verify we can export 30 days of subprocessor access logs in the format in the checklist. Can you confirm by EOD?
- Laura: confirm whether UK Addendum / IDTA-specific fields are already in our current DPA template or require an addendum.
- Jonas: confirm whether the dedicated routing option is feasible for NovaHealth’s EU traffic for the pilot.

I want to give NovaHealth a clear yes/no on conditional start by Wednesday COB. If we can demonstrate the must-have evidence and a signed technical attestation (TIA/DTIA), we can proceed with a limited data scope and monitoring.

Attaching: tia-evidence-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Thanks,
Grace

--
Grace O'Connor
Head of Trust & Compliance, Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182
Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-17T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Conditional TIA acceptance & technical evidence plan — NovaHealth pilot

Grace —

On 2027-05-17 08:12, Grace O'Connor wrote:
> Team —
> 
> Following the call with NovaHealth this morning...

Quick updates:
- Access logs: we can export signature-level and operator-level logs for the last 90 days. The export will be CSV (timestamp, user_id, action, resource). I'm attaching a small sample (subprocessor-access-log-sample.csv) for format review.
- KMS provenance: our KMS team can produce a report of key rotation and ARN ownership (needs a 24h window).
- Subprocessor SLAs: our current subprocessor map shows the affected infra providers; I recommend we provide the redacted map and offer to run a one-off audit snapshot for NovaHealth.

Two points for Legal:
1) If NovaHealth insists on UK IDTA clauses for the UK addendum, we need to confirm which party signs the IDTA (we expect Redwood to be the data importer). Laura — can you advise on standard position?
2) Routing: dedicated routing may add 10% latency but keeps data paths fully in EU. Jonas, can you cost-estimate a one-week proof-of-concept?

I'll ping infra for the KMS report and share by EOD tomorrow.

Vivek

--
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Infrastructure Product, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai | +1 (617) 555-4091
From: Mike Carlton <mike.carlton@novahealth.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Natalie Chen <natalie.chen@novahealth.com>, Emma Bexley <emma.bexley@bexleylegal.com>
Date: 2027-05-18T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Conditional TIA acceptance & technical evidence plan — NovaHealth pilot

Grace / Vivek —

Thanks for the rapid follow-up and the checklist. We can move on a conditional acceptance track but need clarity on two items before we instruct procurement:

1) UK IDTA/UK Addendum: Our security team requires explicit language that no EU->UK routing will occur for EU patient data unless governed by the IDTA or valid SCCs. If Redwood's position is to be the data importer for the IDTA, please confirm who will be the signatory and whether Redwood will accept the standard annex wording.

2) Evidence upload cadence: we can provision a secure SFTP for evidence ingestion. We'd like the must-have evidence in 48 hours and the TIA attestation within 5 business days. Is that reasonable?

We are also copying our outside counsel, Emma, to run a quick read on any DPA addendum language.

If we can get the must-have items, procurement is comfortable issuing a PO for the pilot scope (50k tokens/day) subject to a signed TIA.

Regards,
Mike

--
Mike Carlton
Head of Engineering, NovaHealth
mike.carlton@novahealth.com | +44 20 7946 0183
From: Emma Bexley <emma.bexley@bexleylegal.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Mike Carlton <mike.carlton@novahealth.com>
Cc: Natalie Chen <natalie.chen@novahealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-18T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Conditional TIA acceptance & technical evidence plan — NovaHealth pilot

Grace / Mike —

Please find attached a short evidence request that maps to a TIA/DTIA we would accept for a pilot (bexley-tia-evidence-request.pdf). Key points:

- If Redwood will be the named data importer in the UK Addendum (IDTA), it must accept the specific data routing and subcontractor controls set out in clause 3.1 of the IDTA.
- The SCCs + IDTA combined approach is acceptable for NovaHealth, but we recommend a signed technical attestation from Redwood that covers: encryption key custody, KV cache isolation, and subprocessor access controls.
- Evidence: access logs, KMS key rotation report, subprocessor map, and a signed attestation with corporate signature.

We can accept an initial evidence bundle via secure SFTP followed by DocuSign for the attestation. I've proposed a 5-business-day turnaround for the attestation in the attached.

Attached: bexley-tia-evidence-request.pdf (PDF)

Happy to hop on a short call if you prefer to walk through the checklist.

Best,
Emma

--
Emma Bexley
Partner, Bexley Legal (data protection & privacy)
emma.bexley@bexleylegal.com | +44 20 7000 5555
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Mike Carlton <mike.carlton@novahealth.com>, Emma Bexley <emma.bexley@bexleylegal.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-19T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Conditional TIA acceptance & technical evidence plan — NovaHealth pilot

Mike / Emma —

Thanks — clear asks and timelines. Confirming Redwood position and next steps:

1) Signing party: Redwood will act as the data importer under the UK Addendum (IDTA) for the pilot. We will accept the IDTA clause set for routing and subprocessors as circulated. Laura, please prepare redlined language for Redwood to sign; target: 2027-05-20 COB.

2) Evidence cadence: Vivek's infra team will upload the must-have items to the SFTP by 2027-05-19 COB (access logs sample, KMS rotation report, redwood-subprocessor-map-2027Q1.csv). Vivek, please confirm when upload is complete.

3) Attestation: Legal will prepare a short corporate-level TIA to be signed via DocuSign. We aim to have the DocuSign out by 2027-05-20 and returned by NovaHealth by 2027-05-25.

4) Conditional go-live: Once must-have evidence is confirmed and the TIA is signed, NovaHealth can start the pilot with 50k tokens/day for 14 days. Any regression on evidence (e.g., missing logs) will trigger a pause.

Action items (owner / due):
- Laura Bennett: redline IDTA/UK Addendum and confirm signatory position / 2027-05-20 COB
- Vivek Kulkarni: upload evidence bundle to SFTP / 2027-05-19 COB
- Grace O'Connor: prepare corporate TIA and DocuSign envelope / 2027-05-20 EOD
- Mike / Natalie (NovaHealth): return signed TIA / 2027-05-25

Attachments: redwood-subprocessor-map-2027Q1.csv (for transparency), tia-evidence-checklist.xlsx (previous)

I'll update the HubSpot deal once the DocuSign is out. Thanks everyone — moving to execution.

Best regards,
Grace
